edges.description: Endolysosomal dysfunction and impaired lysosomal Fe2+ mobilization in oligodendrocytes disrupt developmental CNS myelination.
Lysosomal dysfunction in astrocytes and microglia triggers early pro-inflammatory glial reactivity and interferon-pathway upregulation.
Accumulation of phospholipids, mucopolysaccharides, and gangliosides in corneal epithelial lysosomes produces corneal clouding.
Endolysosomal storage and trafficking failure in retinal cells drive early-onset progressive retinal degeneration.
Early CNS hypomyelination and impaired white-matter network maturation manifest in infancy as severe psychomotor developmental delay.
Early central motor-network hypomyelination manifests around one year of age as axial hypotonia.
Deficient developmental commissural myelination produces marked thinning and hypoplasia of the corpus callosum on brain MRI.
Altered thalamocortical white-matter network synchrony is associated with occasional childhood absence seizures despite preserved cortical gray matter.
Chronic axonal hypomyelination compromises trophic support to long descending corticospinal axons.
Chronic pro-inflammatory astrocyte and microglial activation potentiates neuroaxonal and cerebellar injury.
Progressive degeneration of descending corticospinal tracts drives worsening spasticity and spastic quadriparesis.
Corneal epithelial macromolecular storage manifests clinically as bilateral corneal clouding.
Bilateral corneal clouding degrades optical clarity and contributes directly to early visual impairment.
Progressive loss of retinal cellular integrity manifests clinically as retinal degeneration.
Progressive retinal degeneration drives severe visual loss culminating in legal blindness by adolescence.
Early visual deprivation from retinal and corneal pathology combined with central oculomotor dysfunction frequently presents in infancy as strabismus.
Impaired parietal-cell acid secretion results directly in constitutive gastric achlorhydria.
Loss of gastric luminal acidity removes negative feedback on antral G cells, causing marked secondary hypergastrinemia.
Gastric achlorhydria impairs solubilization and intestinal absorption of dietary non-heme iron, leading to iron deficiency anemia.
Absence of gastric acid secretion abolishes luminal acid inhibition of gastrin release.
Gastric achlorhydria impairs intestinal absorption of dietary non-heme iron, causing iron deficiency anemia.

nodes.description: No disease-modifying therapy is approved for MLIV. Management is multidisciplinary and supportive, encompassing developmental and speech services, visual-impairment accommodations and ocular lubrication, surgical strabismus correction, antiseizure medication when needed, feeding support or gastrostomy for dysphagia, annual surveillance (neurologic, ophthalmic, feeding/growth, cystatin C renal function, CBC and iron studies), and avoidance of chloroquine.

evidence.reference_title: Mucolipidosis IV.
evidence.snippet: Treatment of manifestations: Developmental and educational services including speech therapy; physical therapy and bracing for hypotonia and spasticity; intramuscular botulinum toxin injections or oral medications for muscle spasticity and rigidity as needed; anti-seizure medication as needed; surgical correction of strabismus; high-contrast black and white materials for those with visual impairment; topical lubricating eye drops, artificial tears, gels, or ointments for ocular irritation; feeding therapy and/or gastrostomy tube placement may be required for persistent feeding issues

evidence.reference_title: Mucolipidosis IV.
evidence.snippet: Surveillance: Monitor those with seizures and assess for new neurologic manifestations at least annually; assessment of musculoskeletal complications as indicated; monitor developmental progress at least annually; annual ophthalmology examination; feeding and growth evaluation at least annually; cystatin C levels to monitor kidney function at least annually; complete blood count and iron studies annually.

evidence.reference_title: MCOLN1/TRPML1 in the lysosome: a promising target for autophagy modulation in diverse diseases.
evidence.snippet: MCOLN1/TRPML1 is a nonselective cationic channel specifically localized to the late endosome and lysosome. With its property of mediating the release of several divalent cations such as Ca2+, Zn2+ and Fe2+ from the lysosome to the cytosol, MCOLN1 plays a pivotal role in regulating a variety of cellular events including endocytosis, exocytosis, lysosomal biogenesis, lysosome reformation, and especially in Macroautophagy/autophagy.
